The page also binds the parser's failure mode: "If you pass an invalid flag, Claude Code reports the error to stderr before the run starts" (:33).
current: Our non-interactive analogue is the `run` subcommand — help calls it "Spawn server, send message, stream response, exit" (apps/cli/src/index.ts:2044) and it calls `spawnLocalServer(args, { printMode: true })` (index.ts:782, :601-629). Of the thirteen flags the page names, eleven do not exist anywhere in `apps/cli` (grep -a for `permission-mode`, `allowedTools`, `append-system-prompt`, `system-prompt`, `mcp-config`, `plugin-dir`, `plugin-url`, `include-partial-messages`, `forward-subagent-text`, `--agents`, `--settings`, `--continue`, `--resume` over apps/cli/src returns 0 hits each; the only repo-wide `--permission-mode` hits are inside the vendored Claude Agent SDK bundles under apps/electron/{dist/,}resources and packages/pi-agent-server/dist, which spawn the real `claude` binary, not our surface). The permission mode is spelled `--mode` (index.ts:104-106) and its VALUES are already Claude's — `parsePermissionMode` (packages/shared/src/agent/mode-types.ts:241-244) resolves `default/manual/acceptEdits/auto/dontAsk/plan/bypassPermissions` through PERMISSION_MODE_ALIASES (mode-types.ts:209-231). Unrecognized flags are not rejected: parseArgs' `default:` arm pushes any `-`-prefixed token into `rest` (index.ts:160-165), and for `run` `rest` IS the prompt — `cmdRun` does `readPrompt(args.rest, args.rest)` (index.ts:766) and `readPrompt` returns `words.join(' ')` (index.ts:423-424). Verified by executing parseArgs on `run "Fix the lint" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read --append-system-prompt "You are a reviewer"`: `command:"run"`, `mode:""`, `rest:["Fix the lint","--permission-mode","acceptEdits","--allowedTools","Bash,Read","--append-system-prompt","You are a reviewer"]`. With `--mode` unset the session is created at `permissionMode: (...) || 'bypassPermissions'` (index.ts:842). Two of the thirteen have working behaviour under a different (or no) name: `--include-partial-messages` is unconditional — `sendAndStream` writes every `session:event`, text deltas included, whenever `--output-format stream-json` is set (index.ts:457, :469-471) — and subagent text is forwarded unconditionally on that same path, since the `parentToolUseId` guard only applies to the non-stream-json branches (index.ts:481-485), so `--forward-subagent-text`'s opt-in default is inverted. `--continue`/`--resume` have no per-invocation equivalent: `run --no-cleanup` (index.ts:113-115, :788) keeps the session record but `cleanup` still stops the ephemeral server (index.ts:792), and `send <session-id>` requires a separately running server (`--url`, index.ts:2172-2175). There is no session-scoped tool-allow input at all: `CreateSessionOptions` (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:249-283) carries `permissionMode`, `enabledSourceSlugs`, `projectHandleId`, `model`, `llmConnection`, `systemPromptPreset`, `thinkingLevel` and branch fields — no allow-rule, system-prompt-append, MCP, agent, plugin or settings field. The user-facing flag docs list only `--workspace-dir`, `--source`, `--output-format`, `--json-schema`, `--mode`, `--no-cleanup`, `--server-entry` (index.ts:2044-2053; docs/cli.md:163-172, whose `--mode` row still prints the legacy default spelling `allow-all`).
divergence: Three distinct deltas, only one of which is a pure naming problem. (1) NAME ONLY: `--permission-mode` is spelled `--mode`; the accepted values and their semantics already match the page (mode-types.ts:209-231), so this is one `case` label, not a behaviour change. (2) BUILT WRONG: an unrecognized flag is not "reported to stderr before the run starts" (:33) — for `run` it is concatenated into the prompt and the run proceeds at `bypassPermissions` (index.ts:160-165 -> :766 -> :842). So a documented lockdown invocation does not merely fail to lock down; it inverts to the most permissive mode AND feeds the operator's flag text to the model as instructions. (3) NOT BUILT: nine flags have no equivalent input at any layer — `--allowedTools`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt-file`, `--system-prompt`, `--settings`, `--mcp-config`, `--agents`, `--plugin-dir`, `--plugin-url` — because `CreateSessionOptions` (dto.ts:249-283) has no field for any of them; `--source <slug>` covers only part of the source/MCP-enabling axis. `--continue`/`--resume` are also not built for `run`: the near-miss (`run --no-cleanup` then `send`) needs a separate long-lived server, so it is not a headless one-shot equivalent. Two flags are inverted rather than absent: `--include-partial-messages` and `--forward-subagent-text` describe opt-ins whose behaviour we perform unconditionally under `--output-format stream-json` (index.ts:469-471, :481-485), so the flag names are still rejected-into-the-prompt while the default output is wider than the page's.

userImpact: Concrete and permission-widening today. A CI operator who writes the documented lockdown, `nessy-general-agent run "Fix the lint" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read`, gets a run whose prompt is the literal string `Fix the lint --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash,Read` and whose session is created at `bypassPermissions` (index.ts:842) — the most permissive mode, the opposite of what was asked, with no warning on stdout or stderr and exit code 0. The model additionally sees the flag text as part of its instructions. Same shape for `--append-system-prompt "You are a security engineer..."`: the instruction is never applied as a system prompt and instead appears mid-prompt as noise. `--resume "$session_id"` and `--continue` silently start a brand-new session, so a scripted multi-turn review loses its context between calls and the session id lands in the next prompt. `--include-partial-messages` / `--forward-subagent-text` are the mild end: the behaviour a caller wants is already on, so the only damage is the flag text in the prompt — but a consumer relying on the documented default of NOT receiving subagent text gets it unconditionally.
